content_preview.title: Agentic AI Foundation Adds Agent Skills, Open Responses, OpenEnv and OpenSandbox, Taking It From Three Projects at Launch to 10 With 305 Members
content_preview.summary: The Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation says Anthropic, OpenAI, Hugging Face and Alibaba each contributed a project, bringing it to 10 hosted projects and 305 member organizations.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), a Linux Foundation body, [announced on October 22, 2026](https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/agentic-ai-foundation-announces-four-new-projects-agent-skills-open-responses-openenv-and-opensandbox) four new hosted projects: Agent Skills, contributed by Anthropic; Open Responses, contributed by OpenAI; OpenEnv, contributed by Hugging Face; and OpenSandbox, contributed by Alibaba. According to the foundation, the additions bring it to 10 hosted projec...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear News structure (overview, announcement, contributor quotes, Open Responses adoption, membership, unknowns). 744 words by the script count (the writer estimated about 840); within the News range of 400-1200. Includes a 'What We Don't Know' section that states the sourcing limits.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three gzipped snapshots (source-0, source-1, source-2 in sources/2026-10/<slug>/), each HTTP 200, suspicious_patterns null for all. Raw HTML was used for The New Stack (page text via WebFetch is unreliable), and a live re-fetch of all three URLs on 2026-10-24 returned HTTP 200 with the same key strings. source-0 (linuxfoundation.org, 22 Oct 2026, four-projects release): confirms exactly Agent Skills-Anthropic, Open Responses-OpenAI, OpenEnv-Hugging Face, OpenSandbox-Alibaba; 'brings AAIF to 10 hosted projects in its first year, up from its three launch projects in December 2025'; Oct 22-23 AGNTCon + MCPCon North America at the San Jose McEnery Convention Center; the four one-line descriptions quoted verbatim; the six existing projects (A2A, Agent Router, agentgateway, AGENTS.md, goose, MCP) 'all operating under AAIF's open, vendor-neutral governance'; Surtani quote verbatim (CTO and co-founder); David Soria Parra quote verbatim (Co-Creator and Lead Maintainer of MCP, Anthropic); Xiaobin Xu quote verbatim (Head of Development Infrastructure, Alibaba). Arithmetic: 3 launch + 4 new = 7, not 10; the release's own list names 6 existing projects (6 + 4 = 10), so 3 projects joined between December 2025 and now. Neither release says which three or when. The article lists all six and states 'three launch projects' and '10', never claims 3+4, and does not assert when the other three joined, so it states nothing the sources do not support; it does not explicitly explain the gap (minor clarity point, see recommendations). source-1 (linuxfoundation.org, 22 Oct 2026, members release, headline 'Surpasses 300 Members'): 'addition of 7 new Gold Members, 33 new Silver Members, and 18 new Associate Members in the past quarter, bringing total membership to 305 organizations'; summary says '60 new member organizations have joined this quarter'. I counted the lists: 7 Gold, 33 Silver, 18 Associate = 58, so the 60 vs 58 mismatch is real and the article's flag is correct; the release does not explain it. 305 appears in the body and the summary, 300 only in the headline/URL as a milestone, and the article uses 305 correctly. Gold member list, Mozilla Corporation and NIST as Associate members all confirmed. Mazin Gilbert quote verbatim (Executive Director). source-2 (The New Stack, Frederic Lardinois, 22 Oct 2026): 'OpenAI on Thursday announced that it is donating' (22 Oct 2026 is a Thursday); OpenAI spokesperson quote with 'Vercel AI Gateway and Databricks Model Serving already implement it' is verbatim; supporter list (AWS in Bedrock, Databricks, LM Studio, Ollama, Hugging Face, Nvidia, OpenRouter, Red Hat, Vercel, vLLM, OGC previously Llama Stack) matches; Anthropic absent from the list and 'Anthropic is a member of the AAIF' confirmed; Google Interactions API confirmed; 'core schema files are copied from OpenAI's API' confirmed from the contributor guide; 'a technical steering committee, which will initially be made up of project maintainers, handling the technical discussions' confirmed; launch in December 2025 with MCP, goose, AGENTS.md confirmed. Allowlist: linuxfoundation.org (line 175) and thenewstack.io (line 119) are on config/source_allowlist.txt by exact hostname; the www. prefix on the LF URLs resolves to the listed domain. Internal link /article/2026-03/03-linux-foundation-launches-agentic-ai-foundation-to-govern-mcp-and-open-agent-standards-with-anthropic-openai-and-block-as-co-founders resolves to an existing published article (March 2026 launch of AAIF) and is described accurately. All body URLs are in article.sources (body_sources_match passed; no orphans). Independent sourcing: one of three (The New Stack), covering only Open Responses; the article says so itself.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, date, name, title, pairing and quote was checked against the snapshots and held. No fabrication or misattribution found. The headline's 'Three Projects at Launch to 10' and '305 Members' are each directly stated by the Linux Foundation releases. Two facts (project and member counts) rest solely on foundation press releases and are attributed to the foundation in the text ('According to the foundation', 'the foundation said').
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral. Foundation claims are attributed to the Foundation or named speakers, and descriptions are in quote marks and attributed ('is described as'). No promotional adjectives from the releases ('thrilled', 'amazing track record') were adopted. One mildly interpretive phrase ('a lineage relevant to how neutral the specification's origins are') links the New Stack's lineage point to neutrality; it is a reasonable, low-key framing, not a finding.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald coverage of these four project additions or the 305-member milestone. The March 2026 launch article is linked as background only; recent goose and MCP SDK articles are release coverage and do not overlap.
concerns: Conflict of interest, disclosed for the record: Agent Skills is an Anthropic project, and Anthropic makes the model family that powers this newsroom's writer and reviewer (the writer is Claude Sonnet 5.5, as is this reviewer); OpenAI's Open Responses is also covered. I checked for favourable framing and found none: the Anthropic quote is a verbatim attributed donation statement, the article reports that Anthropic is absent from Open Responses supporters, and OpenAI's schema lineage is noted. No claim about Anthropic rests on anything but the cited sources. The article itself carries no reader-facing disclosure of this relationship; the newsroom's general model-disclosure practice applies.

Two of three sources are the Foundation's own press releases (first-party, promotional by nature); the only independent source covers one of the four projects. The article acknowledges this in 'What We Don't Know'.
The release headline/summary says 60 new members while the itemised counts total 58; the article flags this correctly.
recommendations: Optionally state explicitly that the six pre-existing projects minus the three launch projects imply three additions between December 2025 and now, which the sources do not date.
Future AAIF stories would benefit from an independent source on the non-OpenAI projects (Agent Skills, OpenEnv, OpenSandbox).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed News piece with all quotes, numbers and pairings verified against the sources, a correctly flagged 60 vs 58 mismatch, and honest disclosure of limited independent sourcing. Approved without corrections. Featured candidacy: 2 - rival AI vendors moving four agent-stack projects into one neutral foundation is a notable industry-structure shift for a broad developer audience, though sourcing is mostly first-party
